name: Hezekiah
overview: Hezekiah was a male figure noted for his descendants who returned to Judah after the captivity, highlighting his enduring legacy in the post-exilic community. While specific tribal affiliation is not recorded, his role is significant in the restoration period of Judah. No additional personal notes are provided.
namesAndTitles: The name Hezekiah means 'y-h-v-h is [my] strength,' reflecting a personal declaration of reliance on the Lord. This proper name, though not given directly by God, carries a profound theological significance consistent with his biblical portrayal.
familyAndRelationships: Hezekiah is explicitly recorded as an ancestor of Ater, and it is inferred that he is a descendant of Jacob, connecting him to the broader patriarchal lineage of Israel. Beyond these, Scripture does not provide further family details beyond his noted descendants.
scriptureSignificance: Hezekiah's importance in Scripture is underscored by his descendants' return to Judah after captivity, affirming his role in the continuity of God's covenant people. His life and legacy are associated with spiritual revival and trust in God during times of crisis, as reflected in prior accounts of his kingship and reforms. This positions Hezekiah as a model of faithful leadership and divine reliance.
